topic: FORGE AI model architecture open model and organic GTM 2026

questions.question: What AI workflows exist or are planned in FORGE, and which must remain deterministic or human-reviewed?
Which current API models offer the best quality, latency, and cost for each safe workflow?
At what sustained traffic does self-hosting beat API economics and operational risk?
Which open model, license, data, post-training, evaluation, and release plan is viable for public local learning use?
What organic GTM wedge, distribution loops, metrics, experiments, and launch gates fit FORGE?

sources.claim: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Luna standard pricing is $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens; Tier 1 permits 500 RPM and 500k TPM.
sources.note: Current official model page accessed 2026-07-31.

sources.claim: OpenAI current standard prices are Luna $0.20/$1.20, Terra $2/$12, and Sol $5/$30 per million input/output tokens; batch prices are half.
sources.note: Current official pricing page accessed 2026-07-31; supersedes launch-era prices.

sources.claim: Mistral lists Mistral Small 4 at $0.15 input and $0.60 output per million tokens, OCR 4 at $4 per 1,000 pages, Voxtral transcription at $0.003 per minute, and Mistral Embed at $0.10 per million tokens.
sources.note: Official Mistral pricing accessed 2026-07-31.

sources.claim: Gemini 3.6 Flash is $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens, while 3.5 Flash-Lite is $0.30/$2.50.
sources.note: Official current Gemini model guide.

sources.claim: Gemini Developer API clients may not be directed toward or likely accessed by anyone under 18.
sources.note: Official additional terms; decisive for FORGE minor-facing routes.

sources.claim: Claude Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 per million input/output tokens through August 31 2026, then $3/$15; batch is half.
sources.note: Official Anthropic pricing accessed 2026-07-31.

sources.claim: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small costs $0.02 per million input tokens.
sources.note: Official model page.

sources.claim: Runpod lists L4 pods at $0.39 per hour and RTX 4090 pods at $0.69 per hour as of July 27 2026.
sources.note: Official current GPU pricing used for an illustrative raw-cost break-even.

sources.claim: llama.cpp server supports parallel decoding, multi-user service, continuous batching, quantized models, schema-constrained JSON, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
sources.note: Primary project documentation; shows 4-6 requests are a batching problem rather than one-model-per-user.

sources.claim: OLMo 3 7B Instruct is Apache 2.0 and releases code, checkpoints, logs and training details plus SFT, DPO and RLVR stages.
sources.note: Official Ai2 model card; strongest fully open research baseline.

sources.claim: Qwen3.5 9B is an Apache 2.0 multimodal post-trained model compatible with vLLM and SGLang.
sources.note: Official Qwen model card; practical local-quality candidate.

sources.claim: Ministral 3 8B is edge-optimized, multilingual, vision-capable, JSON/function capable, and Apache 2.0.
sources.note: Transformers documentation summarizing the official model family.

sources.claim: OpenAI API data is not used to train models by default; default abuse-monitoring logs may be retained up to 30 days, with stricter controls subject to eligibility.
sources.note: Official provider data-control documentation accessed 2026-07-31.

sources.claim: The IES practice guide supports spacing, active retrieval, delayed judgments of learning, and explanatory questioning, but does not establish FORGE-specific efficacy.
sources.note: Official evidence-practice guide; used only for mechanism rationale.

sources.claim: The 2026 HEPI survey reports very high undergraduate AI use alongside concerns about dependence, skill erosion, unfairness, and isolation.
sources.note: Current independent student survey; supports the anti-answer-engine positioning, not demand or efficacy proof.

sources.claim: The Open Source AI Definition distinguishes open-source AI systems from weights-only releases based on access to preferred forms for modification, data information, code, and parameters.
sources.note: Primary OSI definition; use precise release language.

sources.claim: Hugging Face model cards are designed to disclose intended uses, limitations, training information, evaluation results, and ethical considerations.
sources.note: Primary platform guidance for the public model release package.

sources.claim: Show HN expects something people can run or try and discourages landing pages, sign-up pages, and coordinated voting.
sources.note: Primary launch-channel guidance; use only after a runnable public artifact exists.

sources.claim: Qwen3-4B is Apache 2.0, text-only, supports many languages, and has an official approximately 2.5GB Q4_K_M GGUF release, making it the most accessible practical v0 candidate.
sources.note: Official model card; open-weight rather than fully reproducible because the training corpus is not released.

sources.claim: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is Apache 2.0, multilingual, supports long inputs, and has official GGUF artifacts suitable for local retrieval.
sources.note: Official model card; proposed local RAG component.

sources.claim: OpenStax current textbook licensing guidance requires version-specific review and generally uses noncommercial and share-alike terms that should not be assumed suitable for commercial model training.
sources.note: Primary licensing update; supports a per-item source and rights ledger.
